title: Iron Enrichment at Grain Boundaries in SrTiO3: Does It Stay or Does It Go?
content: Grain boundary dopant adsorption is the positive or negative excess of atoms per unit area of unit interface area in comparison to the adjacent bulk phase. To study the segregation behavior of dopants in, for instance, ceramic microstructures it is of paramount importance to keep dopant concentrations below the respective bulk solubility limits. It is, however, often practiced to intentionally deposit dopants on the free surfaces of ceramic single crystals prior to their diffusion bonding. While this experimental process leads to grain boundary planes enriched with dopant atoms, but the observed interfacial dopant concentration may not reflect an equilibrium interface configuration.
